source_read: https://dimt.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/dim-t-main-menu-allergens-14.08.2026-v1.pdf (V1 14.08.2026, 25 pages, sha256 26e04a828719a675500a0b847e380cc77085e4b72dc6a37cf3fa96b6cc904b4e, fetched 2026-10-08 after an RFC 9309 robots check; matrix pages 2-7 and the page-1 legend read) and, for the dishes' own wording, https://dimt.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/dim-t-main-menu-August-2026.pdf (sha256 fc7a1fbeb8a6277ab9361adc8503bfcdaf8f03c7fa9cd3a2d93dd269df8121f0). The extraction script reproduces data/source/dim-t exactly from these files.
methods: Parser: tools/uk_extract/dim_t_allergen_pdf.py (table grid from a 150 dpi render, word positions from the text layer, header labels checked per column). Independent reading: all 66 published dishes (14 allergen columns, the cereal / nut words and the (F) mark each) compared by eye against the guide's pages 2-7 rendered at 120 dpi: 0 differences (page 2: 10 dishes, page 3: 14, page 4: 13, page 5: 13, page 6: 12, page 7: 4). Run-time self-checks: 130 rows (8 table titles, none with a mark), duplicate guide rows must be identical, every cell word must be an allergen word of its own column, the fryer sentence on page 1 must name all 14 allergens.
notes: Published: 66 of 100 dishes now have allergens.csv rows. Tie: a dish is matched to the ONE guide row with the same words in its name (case, punctuation, '&'=and, '(F)'/'*NEW' marks, plural prawns, word order, Penang=Panang, mien=mein, passionfruit=passion fruit); 42 of the 66 have the same name letter for letter apart from case, 24 differ only in those ways (all 24 pairs are printed by every run). Held back for allergens (26 of 92 published-before dishes, 28%): 19 with no guide row of the same words (NO_ALLERGEN_ROW in dim_t.py, e.g. Five spice squid is 'SPICE SQUID (F)', Wonton soup 'WONTON SOUP WAGYU BEEF', the three ice creams '... ICE CREAM WITH CHOCOLATE SAUCE': the nearest guide row is recorded there for the person who decides; ALIAS in dim_t.py publishes one when approved) and 7 whose row contradicts the chain's own words (policy 3): Stir-fried egg noodles (name says egg, row marks none), the four Chow mein rows (the printed menu says 'wok fried egg noodles', no row marks egg), Phad Thai tofu (the menu's Phad Thai has egg, the other three rows mark it) and Crispy pork belly bao (menu: 'sriracha mayo', row marks no egg). The 8 Thai spicy basil fried rice / Pad kee mao rows were already held back for conflicting calories. The menu's printed (ng) non-gluten marks agree with the guide's gluten column for every dish checked. May contain: the guide prints no per-dish traces list, only that '(F)' dishes are fried and that the fryer oil carries traces of gluten, nuts, peanuts, dairy, soya, sesame, fish, mollusc, crustacean, lupin, egg, mustard, sulphates and celery: the 18 published dishes marked (F) get those 14 as may-contain ('sulphates' is read as sulphites, the 14th allergen; flagged for the founder), the others none; may_contain_published stays yes. Copied as printed, not harmonised: the guide marks (F) on Chow mein beef and tofu but not on chicken and prawn, and 'Coconut' in the Nuts column is kept as nuts with no kind. One medium audit flag logged ok in data/audit/reviewed/dim-t.csv (Singapore fried noodles: no gluten in the guide, '(ng)' on the menu). The menu marks Egg fried rice vegan although the guide marks egg: the guide's egg is published, the vegan mark is not used.
